fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Transhumanism Traced to the Mystery Schools", "body": "Wayne McRoy Jr. opens with a transhumanist documentary that, he says, defines the movement as eugenics without coercion, and he argues eugenics sits at its core. He traces the same ambitions of immortality, godhood and total control back to the old mystery schools and secret societies, now within reach because of modern technology. He also claims that public technology such as Neuralink and brain computer interfaces trails black budget programs by decades. Chance frames the conversation around Wayne's book, Cybernetic Messiah, and its warning against letting technocrats decide the future."}, {"title": "Secrecy, Fire, and the First Priest-King", "body": "Wayne offers an allegory in which the first person to keep a fire burning gained a special place as priest, scientist and king, and kept the secret from the ignorant, passing it only to a chosen son. He argues that secrecy and a knowledge differential became the root of class division and remain a mind control tool today. Chance adds that the same group could next command eclipses. Both discuss Lucifer and Prometheus as a gift of light that was later inverted, and Wayne insists that intention is what empowers any symbol."}, {"title": "Legal Fictions and Artificial Worlds", "body": "Chance reads Wayne's line about artificial worlds created in the minds of men, then connects it to the idea of worldviews filtered through other people's ideas until little contact with reality remains. Wayne points to the legal fiction behind a driver's license, a bank account and a social media identity, plus the drift toward digital currency, and names religion, philosophy, mythology and science as four foundations of control. He says people who miss mythology also miss the social engineering in stories like Star Wars. Chance sees a gnostic cage retranslated as simulation theory."}, {"title": "Elementals, Egregores, and Revealed Methods", "body": "Answering Chance's question about elementals in orders such as the OTO and Golden Dawn, Wayne traces the idea through the Rosicrucians to Paracelsus, who he says meant natural energies, and to a book he describes as satire that occultists took seriously. He argues that, through the Hermetic principle of mentalism, concentrated belief can make a tulpa or egregore feel real. Chance wonders whether the Grand Architect is an artificial demiurge, and Wayne describes revelation of the method, crediting Michael Hoffman and James Shelby Downard, with his own reading of 9/11 as the example."}, {"title": "Stepping Out in Faith", "body": "Chance closes the free hour by asking about a recent leap of faith, and Wayne describes leaving a long, stressful job with no backup plan after thought and prayer. He says a suitable position appeared the very next day and called him back right away, with flexible hours and less stress. He frames it as a testimony that honoring a calling opens doors where there were none. Chance replies that the podcast itself began from the same inspiration, and that following your deepest wish brings help from unseen forces."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Wayne McRoy Jr. of Alchemical Tech Revolution joins us to shed light on the technocratic agenda, inspire us towards positive leaps of faith, and help us comprehend the fractal, spiritual, and physical dynamics employed by social engineers to alter human behavior, physiology, and worldviews. Topics include transhumanism, AI egregores, artificial synchronicity, secret societies and their dogmatic mysteria, and tons more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Cybernetics Means Steering Whole Systems", "body": "Chance opens the members hour by asking what cybernetics means, and Wayne explains the Greek root kybernetes, meaning steersman or pilot, and defines the field as the study of systems control. Chance stresses that it covers life as well as machines, a sort of forced evolution, and Wayne cites Norbert Wiener's phrasing about animal and machine. Wayne also claims that many technologies are dual use, vetted by the military for decades before reaching the public, with the phone as his example, and Chance adds a claim that iPhones capture infrared images of the face."}, {"title": "Compartmentalization, Homeostasis, and the Causal Circuit", "body": "Wayne contrasts schooling that splits knowledge into compartments, using a podiatrist and a car assembly line, with the cyberneticist who sees the whole system. He then explains Walter Cannon's homeostasis, the thermostat analogy and feedback loops, and says that introducing a new stimulus creates a causal circuit through which a system can be hijacked. He claims modern data lets controllers model outcomes at ninety eight or ninety nine percent accuracy. Chance contributes a sweat and thirst example of multi-dimensional feedback and calls compartmentalization a broken feedback loop."}, {"title": "Distributed Intelligence Versus the Machine", "body": "Chance and Wayne agree that the body runs on distributed intelligence while computers route everything back to a central processor, so the Internet of Things looks to them like a cheap knockoff. Wayne argues the controllers are trying to pare human intelligence down to machine parity through the singularity and brain computer interfaces such as Neuralink, and he fears a spiritual gateway for something malevolent. He also describes metaphysical consent, comparing it to inviting a vampire in, and says entertainment announces agendas in advance. Chance adds a video game plot about implanted AI."}, {"title": "The Superego, the Veil, and the Matrix", "body": "Chance proposes that the superego, the voice of the crowd in the head, may be the original artificial intelligence implant, cutting people off from their authentic self. Wayne maps body, mind and spirit, calling the mind the veil or abyss that sits between the physical and the spiritual, which is why he says controllers target it with mind control technology. Chance has a flash that the mind is a matrix, meaning womb, and Wayne calls the control scheme an inversion that turns what is internal into something external."}, {"title": "Entropy, Centropy, and a Way Forward", "body": "Wayne argues that nature always self-corrects, pointing to the regrowth at Chernobyl, and that the larger and more complex a control system grows, the more maintenance it demands until it collapses under its own weight. Chance, citing an IT background, adds that more complexity needs more people to keep it running, and names centropy as the self-organizing counterpart to entropy. Both close on practical hope: Wayne's motto is to do the right thing and trust the creator, and Chance urges reducing dependency on these systems and untraining the mind from authority."}]
